milestone: All 26 published packages verified end to end through npx, and one mirror trap found and documented
method: npx --yes --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org PKG@latest <sample>, per package, checking that the bin resolves and the tool runs. An exit code of 1 (findings) is success; 127/E-NOENT/'could not determine executable' is failure.

result.note: dsh-hashcheck needs a subcommand (build/verify); invoked with a bare path it prints usage and exits 2, which is by design. Verified properly with build then verify: both exit 0.

finding.symptom: npx dsh-dockerfile-check failed with 'could not determine executable to run' while the package was demonstrably on npm
finding.root_cause: the default registry in ~/.npmrc is npmmirror; for the two packages published that same hour the mirror had the tarball but a manifest whose bin field had not synced yet. npx reads bin from the manifest to decide what to execute, so it could not choose.
finding.discrimination_test: the same two packages run correctly against registry.npmjs.org — so this is a mirror sync window, not a package defect
finding.why_it_matters: the error reads like a broken package. A user in China with a default mirror would conclude the tool does not work and move on, which is the worst outcome for a package whose only job is to be run once to prove it works
finding.documented: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md section 7, published at /troubleshooting/, with the discriminating command and the hashcheck subcommand note

verification_chain_now: npx run of the published artifact
